tip: fare la spesa is the set phrase for grocery shopping: faccio la spesa. The plural fare le spese means clothes shopping.
Adjectives ending in -e use -i for the plural in both genders: felici = happy, from felice.
potrei is the polite could I: potrei avere il menu? = could I have the menu, softer than posso.
Potremmo, the conditional of potere, makes a request polite: potremmo avere il conto? = could we have the bill? gentler than possiamo.
Frutta is a feminine collective noun and stays singular even for many pieces: più frutta = more fruit, not 'frutte'.
Add -mente to an adjective to make an adverb, like English -ly: lento becomes lentamente = slowly.

english: He knows how to cook well.
tip: sapere plus an infinitive means to know how to: sa cucinare = he can cook. potere would mean is allowed to.

english: We would like to order dessert.
tip: Vorremmo is the polite 'we would like', softer than vogliamo (we want): vorremmo ordinare = we would like to order.

english: They say it would rain tomorrow.
tip: The conditional can flag unconfirmed news: pioverebbe = 'supposedly it will rain', marking it as merely reported, not certain.

english: Do you know what time it is?
tip: Telling time is plural: che ore sono? = what time is it, answered sono le tre. Only one o'clock is singular: e l'una.

english: On Mondays I work a lot.
tip: 'Molto' as adverb is invariable: 'lavoro molto' (I work a lot). As adjective it agrees: 'molte persone' (many people).

english: I would gladly eat a pizza.
tip: Verbs ending in -giare drop the i in the future and conditional: mangiare becomes Mangerei, never mangierei.

english: It would be better to leave early.
tip: Sarebbe meglio plus an infinitive softens advice: sarebbe meglio partire = 'it would be better to leave', gentler than a flat command.
Lungo means 'long' as an adjective but 'along' before a noun: cammino lungo il fiume = I walk along the river.
Vicino needs a after it: abitiamo vicino al parco. English 'near the park' has no preposition, but Italian adds the a.

english: She gets ready to go out.
tip: Italian makes routine verbs reflexive: si prepara = she prepares herself (gets ready), where English just says 'gets ready'.

english: The dog runs in the garden.
tip: 'In' contracts with articles: in+il=nel, in+la=nella. 'Nel giardino' = in the garden. Mandatory with definite articles.

english: In the evening I watch a movie.
tip: An article on a time word signals a habit: la sera guardo un film = in the evenings, every evening, I watch a movie.

target: La metro passa ogni cinque minuti.
english: The metro comes every five minutes.
tip: Ogni never changes form, and before a number it takes a plural noun: ogni cinque minuti = every five minutes.

target: Dubito che lui sappia la risposta.
english: I doubt he knows the answer.
tip: Sapere has an irregular subjunctive, sappia, used after dubito che: dubito che lui sappia.

target: È necessario che tu faccia attenzione.
english: It's necessary that you pay attention.
tip: Fare attenzione, literally 'to make attention', means to pay attention: faccia attenzione.

target: Noi passiamo le vacanze al mare.
english: We spend the holidays at the beach.
tip: Spending time is passare; spendere is only for money. Passiamo le vacanze = we spend the holidays.
Stare covers how you are doing: sta peggio di ieri = she is feeling worse than yesterday. Health and mood take stare.
Italian uses stare, not essere, for body position: stiamo seduti = we are sitting.
Ci vediamo is literally we see each other, the normal way to say see you later.
The object pronoun can sit before the modal or attach to the infinitive: mi puoi aiutare = puoi aiutarmi, both fine.
servire works like piacere: in ti serve aiuto, aiuto is the subject and ti is who needs it.
Cos'hai is cosa + hai: cosa drops its final -a before the vowel of hai. Cos'hai fatto = what did you do.
uscire takes da for leaving a place: esce dal lavoro = he leaves work.
Lateness is a fixed phrase with essere: essere in ritardo = to be late, so siamo in ritardo.
